nodes.content: Develop simultaneous speech translation that preserves late-resolved negation and semantic roles while committing irreversible output under bounded latency.
requirements: Achieve at least 20% fewer negation and role errors than a matched-latency streaming baseline.
Keep average lagging below two seconds without reducing overall COMET versus the same baseline.

nodes.content: Use source-conditioned role–polarity lattices and a 1.5-second adaptive commit gate to emit only prefixes invariant across plausible continuations.
How can the decoder identify irreversible target prefixes that survive late-arriving negators and role disambiguation within the 1.5-second gate?
Within the 1.5-second gate, committing prefixes shared across a calibrated 95%-mass lattice yields ≥97% role–polarity prefix correctness.
On 600 CoVoST2 Japanese–English utterances, measure 95%-mass lattice prefix role–polarity correctness, AL, and COMET against matched-latency baselines with 1.5-second gates.
On 600 Japanese–English CoVoST2 utterances, 1.5-second-gated prefixes reached 97.4% role–polarity correctness versus 94.0% baseline; AL 1.8s, COMET 78.3 versus 78.1.
Retain the 95%-mass, 1.5-second gate for broader testing: prefix correctness exceeds 97% while AL and COMET meet constraints.
With the retained 1.5-second gate, calibrate 95%-mass lattices by clause type and test invariant-prefix commits on late-negation/role-swap subsets.
Calibrate clause-stratified lattices on 400 additional CoVoST2 utterances; test gated commits on 200 disjoint late-negation/role-swap cases for errors, AL, COMET.
ClauseCal-v1 bundles 400-utterance clause-stratified calibrators, 200-case late-negation/role-swap annotations, and gated-versus-baseline error, AL, and COMET tables.
Audit ClauseCal-v1’s 200-case annotations and recompute clause-wise lattice coverage, gated negation/role errors, AL, and COMET against baseline.
On ClauseCal-v1’s 200-case audit, gated/baseline errors were 9/12 negation and 13/18 role; AL 1.86s; COMET 77.9/77.7.
Clause-specific negator and case-marker hazard scores will catch ≥80% of unsafe 95%-mass commits while keeping AL below 2s.
Fit clause-specific negator/case-marker hazards on ClauseCal-v1’s 400 utterances; test unsafe-commit recall and AL on 300 held-out late-cue cases.
On 300 held-out late-cue cases, hazard scores flagged 19/25 unsafe commits (76% recall), below 80%; AL was 1.89s.
Add late-cue forecasts to the lattice gate; test ≥20% fewer negation/role errors, AL <2s, and nondecreasing COMET on CoVoST2.
Integrate a clause-conditioned late-cue forecast into the 95%-mass gate and benchmark it against matched-latency streaming on 1,000 CoVoST2 utterances.
LateCueGate-v1 contains clause-conditioned forecast weights, a 95%-mass commit decoder, and 1,000-utterance CoVoST2 matched-latency benchmark logs.
Use clause-aware reordering to emit role-neutral lead-ins, delaying polarity and agent–patient commitments under a 1.8-second lag budget.
How can clause-aware reordering defer agent–patient and polarity decisions without producing ungrammatical English or exceeding 1.8 seconds?
Constrained role-neutral English lead-ins will reduce negation/role errors ≥20% while preserving ≥95% grammaticality, AL <1.8s, and baseline COMET.
Using LateCueGate-v1’s 1,000-utterance CoVoST2 logs, compare lattice-only, role-neutral, combined, and matched-latency baseline decoders: errors, grammaticality, AL, COMET.
On 1,000 utterances, lattice-only cut baseline negation/role errors 25% (AL 1.78s, COMET 78.3/78.1); role-neutral grammaticality was 92%.
Advance lattice-only LateCueGate-v1: its 25% error reduction meets constraints; defer role-neutral lead-ins because 92% grammaticality misses 95%.
When retained LateCueGate-v1 stalls, syntax-verified role-neutral lead-ins should yield ≥95% grammaticality, ≥20% fewer errors, AL <1.8s, and nondecreasing COMET.
Implement syntax-verified lead-ins at LateCueGate-v1 stalls; compare with lattice-only and matched-latency baseline on errors, grammaticality, AL, COMET.
On 1,000 CoVoST2 utterances, syntax-verified stall lead-ins achieved 96% grammaticality, 28% fewer negation/role errors versus baseline, AL 1.76s, COMET 78.4/78.1.
Extend the validated syntax-verified stall lead-ins to held-out CoVoST2 speakers; audit clause-wise grammaticality, polarity/role errors, AL, and COMET.
Stream 500 speaker-disjoint CoVoST2 utterances through syntax-verified stall gating; score clause-wise grammaticality, negation/role errors, AL, and COMET versus baseline.
SpeakerHoldout-500 contains speaker-disjoint audio, irreversible output timestamps, clause labels, grammaticality judgments, and baseline-comparative error, AL, and COMET scores.
Audit SpeakerHoldout-500 against ClauseCal-v1 clause strata, measuring calibration drift, grammaticality, negation/role errors, AL, and COMET versus baseline.
On SpeakerHoldout-500, stall lead-ins yielded 95.6% grammaticality and 23% fewer negation/role errors; AL 1.79s, COMET 77.8/77.6 versus baseline.
Adopt syntax-verified stall lead-ins with LateCueGate-v1: ClauseCal-v1 gate audits and held-out tests show ≥23% fewer errors without latency/COMET regressions.
Train a streaming encoder with counterfactual negator and case-marker swaps to sharpen polarity/role predictions before irreversible commits.
Generate aligned negator/case-marker counterfactuals, retrain the streaming encoder, then compare adopted-gate errors, AL, and COMET on fresh speaker-disjoint CoVoST2.
Use LateCueGate-v1 commit logs to align 2,000 negator/case-marker-swapped Japanese utterances; fine-tune the streaming encoder with role–polarity contrastive loss.
SwapEnc-v1 packages 2,000 aligned Japanese negator/case-marker counterfactuals, role–polarity contrastive training code, and fine-tuned streaming encoder weights.
Does SwapEnc-v1's counterfactual training reduce natural speaker-disjoint late-cue errors without degrading COMET or exceeding 2-second AL?
With the adopted gate, SwapEnc-v1 cuts speaker-disjoint negation/role errors ≥10% versus the original encoder, with AL <2s and nondecreasing COMET.
Compare SwapEnc-v1 and original encoders on 600 fresh speaker-disjoint CoVoST2 utterances with adopted gates; score negation/role errors, AL, COMET.
On 600 speaker-disjoint utterances, SwapEnc-v1 reduced adopted-gate negation/role errors from 62 to 54 (12.9%); AL 1.83s, COMET 78.0/77.8.
Adopt SwapEnc-v1 with the retained gate: 12.9% fewer errors than the original encoder, AL 1.83s, and COMET improves 0.2.
Ablate SwapEnc-v1 and syntax-verified lead-ins under adopted gating on 800 fresh speaker-disjoint CoVoST2 utterances; measure errors, grammaticality, AL, COMET.
On 800 speaker-disjoint utterances, SwapEnc-v1 plus lead-ins cut original-encoder errors 64→56 (baseline 80); grammaticality 96%, AL 1.84s, COMET 78.2/78.0.
Do counterfactual swaps overfit synthetic cue positions, leaving naturally delayed negators or case markers unsafe to commit?
On naturally delayed cues, SwapEnc-v1 reduces original-encoder negation/role errors ≥10%, approaching its 12.9% speaker-disjoint reduction.
Compare adopted-gate SwapEnc-v1 and the original encoder on 300 naturally late-cued CoVoST2 utterances: negation/role errors by cue position, AL, COMET.
On 300 naturally late-cued utterances, SwapEnc-v1 made 38 errors versus 35 original and 44 baseline; AL 1.86s, COMET 77.5/77.7.
Defer SwapEnc-v1 despite aggregate gains: natural late cues worsen errors and COMET; retain original encoder with lattice gate and lead-ins.
Validate retained original-encoder lattice gating and syntax-verified lead-ins on speaker-disjoint late-cue CoVoST2: errors, AL, COMET versus matched-latency baseline.
Use SpeakerHoldout-500 labels to stratify 600 new speaker-disjoint late-cue utterances; compare retained system and matched-latency baseline on errors, AL, COMET.
SpeakerHoldout-1100 revises SpeakerHoldout-500 with 600 additional speaker-disjoint late-cue utterances, stratified annotations, and retained-system/baseline error, AL, COMET logs.
Audit SpeakerHoldout-1100’s 600 new cases by ClauseCal-v1 strata; ablate lattice gate and syntax-verified lead-ins against matched-latency baseline: errors, AL, COMET.
On 600 late-cue cases, baseline/lattice/full negation/role errors were 100/84/76; full AL was 1.85s, COMET 77.9/77.7 (full/baseline).
Finalize original-encoder lattice gate plus syntax-verified lead-ins: 24% fewer late-cue errors, AL 1.85s, COMET +0.2; exclude SwapEnc-v1.
